title: Skeleton: games/dusk-helm with input, actor, physics and world interfaces
addendum:
Engineering ticket (no creator review). Beyond the stubs, the skeleton must give every later rung its hooks:
- **Scenario loader**: `?scenario=<id>` reads `games/dusk-helm/scenarios/<id>.json` (seed, area, class, build, enemies, inventory), so prototypes and playtests open straight onto their moment (gm-new-game-plan `prototype-ladder.md`).
- **Manifest**: declare `move` as a **stick** plus at most five buttons, most-used first (rule 27; the 2D scaffold's `axis` gives phones no controls). Declare `modes` (one per class, with exact tap paths) and `playArea.tap` for `gm qa playtest --all-modes` and `gm look shell` (rules 41–42).
- Mark the world canvas `data-gm-play-area`. Put `user-select:none; -webkit-touch-callout:none` on `html, body`. Add an empty `qa.invariants()` hook that later tickets extend (rule 31, 42).
- Create `design/feedback.json`, `review/decisions.json` and `review/` evidence folders so `gm options check` and `gm look check` have something to read (11-09: an absent decisions file let every look pass).
- Keep player state in `players: Map` with no singleton player (gm-multiplayer-ready), even though multiplayer is out of scope.
- Done also needs `gm check boot --dist dist` green at 390x844, plus the title rendering in a clean-clone production build (rule 43).

Shared rules: `docs/plans/dusk-helm-learnings/learnings.md` in the core repo (rule numbers above refer to it).

title: Foundation proof: assembled village fragment, correct scale, depth order and collision

They differ in time of day and palette, camera zoom, HUD shape and building density (rule 4). Describe the SmallScaleInt kit in words; never attach pack renders (rule 23). Mark them AI-generated.
- **Prototype rung**: the assembled fragment in the engine, from the same camera, beside the picked mock. Include the feasibility list (each element mapped to a card id or marked a gap, rule 7) and a `gm look score/judge` sheet. Plateau rule 14.
